title: Reproduction in Humans
seo_title: Primary 5 Science: Reproduction in Humans Worksheets (with Answers)
standard_code: Primary 5: Cycles in plants and animals (Reproduction in humans)
standard_text: Identify the organs of the human male and female reproductive systems and their functions: the testes produce sperms and the ovaries produce eggs. Describe fertilisation as the joining of a sperm and an egg, and that the fertilised egg develops into a baby in the womb. Recognise that characteristics are passed down from parents to their children (summary of the MOE Primary Science Syllabus).
meta_desc: Free Primary 5 science worksheets for Singapore pupils on human reproduction: testes and ovaries, sperms and eggs, fertilisation, the womb, and inherited characteristics. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: A sperm and an egg join to start a new life.
key_sub: The baby develops in the womb for about 9 months.
body_html:
How to think about it

Humans reproduce sexually: a sperm from the father joins with an egg from the mother.

  • The testes make sperms. The ovaries make eggs.
  • Fertilisation is the joining of a sperm and an egg.
  • The fertilised egg develops into a baby in the womb for about 9 months, getting food and oxygen through the umbilical cord.
  • Children inherit characteristics from both parents. Scars, haircuts and languages are not inherited.
Example

Where are eggs made?

Eggs are female reproductive cells

They are made in the ovaries

Answer: In the ovaries.

Example

A father has a scar. Will his baby have it?

A scar happens during life

It is not inherited

Answer: No.

Common mistakes

  • Thinking the baby grows in the mother's stomach. It grows in the womb.
  • Mixing up the testes and the ovaries.
  • Thinking a child gets all its characteristics from one parent. It inherits from both.
  • Thinking scars, tans or languages can be inherited.

faq.a: Inside the mother's body, when a sperm joins with an egg. The fertilised egg then develops in the womb.

faq.q: How does a baby get food in the womb?
faq.a: Through the umbilical cord, which carries food and oxygen from the mother's blood to the baby.
Characteristics such as eye colour, dimples, the shape of the earlobes and tongue rolling are inherited from both parents. Scars, haircuts and languages are not.
